findings.title: Legacy mode bypasses trusted identity and reviewed activity admission.
findings.context: Legacy mode parses caller claims locally. It does not verify signatures, issuer trust, or expiration. It injects direct Mastery and enables the legacy activity fallback.
evidence: A fileless probe accepted an identity with exp=1 and resolved a Mastery tenant.
The fallback accepts sales.value-proposition and quiz.recognition even though the current Sales binding package has no such coordinate.
The restored Red projection suite uses legacy mode, so its valid projection does not prove the trusted boundary.
findings.impact: A caller can use an expired or forged claim and unreviewed evidence to mutate Mastery through the public projection seam.
findings.required_fix: Remove legacy mode from the production export, or require the verifier and scoped factory in every mode. Remove the legacy fallback.

findings.title: Source attempts are not bound to immutable Sales attempt records.
findings.context: sourceAttemptId only requires a nonblank string. The projection does not resolve an immutable quiz attempt or roleplay evaluation owned by the verified organization and principal.
evidence: The source uses input.sourceAttemptId as audit.sourceId and as the Mastery submissionId.
Roleplay evaluator attemptId and attemptDigest are shape-checked but are not matched to sourceAttemptId or a stored attempt.
The current pending roleplay state blocks current roleplay projection, but fabricated quiz attempt identities remain accepted.
findings.impact: An authorized caller can submit a fabricated attempt identity with an approved coordinate and create mastery evidence.
findings.required_fix: Resolve the immutable source attempt server-side. Verify its organization, principal, activity, result, and release before projection.

findings.title: Mastery commit and Sales receipt insertion are separate transactions.
findings.context: ensureBindingAndOutbox commits mapping and outbox rows first. deliverDatabase then commits Mastery and inserts the Sales receipt in separate operations.
evidence: insertReceipt calls the root database insert after the Mastery adapter transaction returns.
A process failure between these calls leaves a Mastery commit without a Sales receipt.
findings.impact: The durable projection can lose its receipt boundary after an applied Mastery mutation. Retry recovery cannot guarantee one atomic projection record.
findings.required_fix: Use a shared transaction-capable Mastery boundary for Mastery rows, the commit, the receipt, and the outbox, or add an explicit durable delivery protocol.
